title: ShoulderPain — Research-Backed Shoulder & Scapula Pain Guide
description: Source-linked GitHub Pages guide to shoulder and shoulder-blade ('wing') pain, written around one stated context — a male adult aged about 36-40, left-side sleeping, a possible workout injury, prolonged computer use and limited room space — and explicitly educational information rather than a diagnosis or a personalised rehabilitation plan, with emergency and urgent warning signs given priority over exercises, furniture or symptom logging. Ten pages share one static template and compact navigation: start, medical advice, treatment, exercises, desk and room, furniture and prices, care costs, an optional log, sources and audit, and next steps; all research content works without JavaScript and no sign-in or symptom entry is required. The current revision is a deliberate narrowing rather than an expansion. It reviewed the pre-existing site at commit e1c63c4 and, in its own words, 'replaces blanket verification/completeness claims with a narrower, auditable source register, simplifies the UI and corrects unsafe or unverified assumptions', keeping the previous site in Git history. Twenty official pages were opened directly on 2026-09-20 — MedlinePlus, NHS, AAOS/ASES, CSP, OSHA, CMS, five furniture manufacturers or sellers, and Luna — and data/sources.json records each source's section, a short excerpt, its scope and its check date, with government and medical-society guidance kept separate from commercial product information. data/claims.json maps source-bearing content units to references and source-file lines: 90 review units, described as a review aid and 'not an automated truth certificate'. Exercises were reduced to four source-checked examples carrying exact AAOS HTML doses and supervision boundaries. Five furniture listings give exact variant and price boundaries with folding trade-offs, and no product is claimed to fit an unmeasured room or to treat shoulder pain; the one care price quoted is an official provider example ($135 self-pay per visit at Luna), not a nationwide average, and other unverified medical costs are explicitly left unpriced. REVIEW.md documents three passes and eight source irregularities found while reading, including a COMHOMA price where $54.49 was the selected White variant and $25.50 the discount, a VIVO desk that folds against the wall but is not quickly detached, a Lillipad whose specifications claim a 700 lb static test while its FAQ says 350 lb and neither replaces the 75 lb operational rating, and a Luna search excerpt showing $125 where both directly opened pages showed $135. The optional log is local-only, retains the `shoulderpain-log-v1` key so prior entries can still be read or imported if valid, and validates numbers, booleans, calendar dates and shape; invalid entries are counted and never rounded or silently converted, invalid persisted data blocks edits rather than being overwritten, raw JSON export is available for recovery, cross-tab changes block saves until reload, spreadsheet formula injection is mitigated on CSV export, and the bounded import size was raised to 20 MB so the 5,000-entry schema can import its own backups. Its former clinical 'improving/worsening' classifier and calendar-based advice were removed on the grounds that sparse logs should not reassure someone or postpone assessment, and the summary is now descriptive only. Validation reports 8 Node unit tests and 31 Chromium browser tests passing, automated axe WCAG 2 A/AA and 2.1 AA checks passing on all ten pages at 390px and 1440px, and no page-level horizontal overflow at 320, 390, 768 or 1440px. Sources retrieved 2026-09-20.

flags: Its own verification policy refuses the strongest claims a directory reader might assume: 'Unknown or conflicting facts stay visibly unresolved. No claim of independent clinical verification or zero errors', and 'Automated checks cannot establish medical accuracy'. REVIEW.md adds that no clinician independently reviewed the personalised suitability of the information, and that link integrity, automated accessibility and browser tests are not medical validation.

Deliberately narrower than the version it replaced. The prior revision carried a 56-source register (S1-S56), four logged review passes, 32 logged corrections and a 32-row irregularity table; this one carries 20 opened sources, three passes, 8 source irregularities and a 6-row next-steps table. Its stated reason is worth quoting because it is the opposite of the usual instinct: 'The guide is a focused, source-linked starting set, not all possible diseases or products. Further expansion should improve evidence rather than inflate a count' (IRR-57).

Now has a build and test step, unlike the version previously described here: npm ci, npm run build (claim ledger plus ten static root HTML pages), npm run check, npm test, npm run test:browser (Playwright) and npm run serve, with the shared page layout in tools/build.py and Python 3 and Node 22 used in validation. Visitors need neither. Committed root HTML means the Pages configuration needs no runtime build.

Browser tests were run against an npm-distributed Chromium 153 binary extracted outside Git because the standard Playwright browser download and Debian package retrieval were blocked by sandbox networking; REVIEW.md states plainly that 'this is not an unexecuted test claim', and CI uses the normal Playwright installation on GitHub-hosted runners. Remaining testing limits it names: no manual screen-reader-user audit, no cross-browser matrix, no third-party video-playback test, and automated accessibility is not full conformance certification.

Open limitations it lists for a next session: no clinician exam or clinical peer review and no systematic literature review; actual room fit, safe removal route and body/desk measurements unknown; no checked chair meets both the folding and the adjustable long-day-workstation criteria; product stock, prices and return policies change and Lillipad has contradictory page content; personal care and medicine costs, country and insurance remain unknown.

Changed state four times inside one audit and this description is the fourth rewrite — verified in sequence against 239eaa8 (01:25:47Z), dd1a7d4 (02:13:17Z), 6812ef3 (02:42:19Z, 60 seconds after a prior stamp had been written) and now 8a21b94 (03:07:51Z), which rebuilt all ten pages and reversed the sourcing method entirely (IRR-47, IRR-57).

Re-verified upstream on 21 September 2026: every medical, exercise and workstation source (M1-M6, E1-E3, W1-W3) was re-opened and all registered excerpts still match the official pages. Product rechecks succeeded only partially — VIVO and Lillipad were re-verified through official seller product-data endpoints, while fetch-proxy failures prevented re-opening IKEA, Branch, three manual/spec PDFs and the cost sources, whose entries stay dated 20 September 2026 and are labelled as such on the site. No price, stock or fit fact was invented for the items that could not be re-opened.
